title: Integrable Fourier moments give a representative of the specified L2 class
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on $\mathbf R^m$, $m\geq1$. Let $u\in L^2(\mathbf R^m;\mathbf C)$, the space of measurable square-integrable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality, and let $h$ be a measurable representative of its Plancherel Fourier transform, defined as the continuous $L^2$ extension of $f\mapsto(\xi\mapsto\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}f(x)\,dx)$ on Schwartz functions (smooth functions with all derivatives rapidly decreasing). Let $r\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose $\int\|\xi\|^j|h(\xi)|\,d\xi<\infty$ for every integer $0\leq j\leq r$. The absolutely convergent integral $$g(x)=\int_{\mathbf R^m}e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}h(\xi)\,d\xi$$ defines a $C^r$ complex-valued function on $\mathbf R^m$, and $g=u$ almost everywhere, so the $L^2$ class of $g$ is the specified class $u$.

source.place: WANTED locally; VI §2, Sobolev lemma (2.1), printed p.289. The inverse-Fourier moment argument for (2.1), including identification with the original almost-everywhere class. Agent-stated supporting lemma, not a separately numbered assertion of Demailly. Supporting code read: Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/Sobolev.lean:212–275; Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/LpSpace.lean:47–139; Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/FourierTransformDeriv.lean:498–524, 703–707. Online statement read in https://totomityann.github.io/pdf/lua_agbook.pdf, VI §2 (2.1), PDF page 152 (a recomposed excerpt, not the original pagination).

proof.text: The moment assumption for $j=0$ says $h\in L^1$. Since $|e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}h(\xi)|=|h(\xi)|$, the integral defining $g$ converges absolutely for every $x$. Apply [lem-sfb-bilinear-fourier-moment-regularity] with $a=b=m$, $f=h$, and $L(\xi,x)=-\xi\cdot x$. This is a continuous real bilinear form, and its negative-exponent Fourier integral is exactly $g$. All its moment hypotheses are the stated hypotheses, so $g$ is $C^r$, also when $r=0$.

source.place: 507-514; specialization to the negative inner product.

proof.text: Choose a measurable representative $u_0$ of the given $L^2$ class $u$. By [lem-sfb-lp-local-integrability] at $p=2$, $u_0$ is locally integrable. Step 1 gives continuity of $g$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-local-integrability] with $U=\mathbf R^m$ and $f=g$ to see that $g$ is locally integrable as well. The whole Euclidean space is open; both functions are measurable.

source.place: 351-358 and 566-569; local integrability of L2 and continuous functions.

proof.text: Let $\psi:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R$ be any smooth compactly supported test, and regard it as the complex function $q=\psi+i0$. By [lem-sfb-schwartz-test-inclusion-integrability], $q$ is Schwartz and belongs to $L^1$. Apply [lem-sfb-l1-bilinear-fourier-duality] to $h,q$ and $L(\xi,x)=-\xi\cdot x$. Its two $L^1$ hypotheses hold by step 1 and the preceding sentence. The transpose is the same negative inner-product phase, hence $J_{L^{\mathrm t}}q=\mathcal Gq$, and it gives $\int g(x)q(x)\,dx=\int h(\xi)(\mathcal Gq)(\xi)\,d\xi$. On the other hand, apply [lem-sfb-l2-inverse-fourier-test-duality] with $v=\mathcal F_2u$, representative $v_0=h$, and test $q$. Its inverse law says $\mathcal G_2v=u$, so $w_0=u_0$ is a permitted representative. It gives $\int q(x)u_0(x)\,dx=\int(\mathcal Gq)(\xi)h(\xi)\,d\xi$. Commutativity of complex multiplication now yields $\int\psi(x)g(x)\,dx=\int\psi(x)u_0(x)\,dx$. This proves the test identity for every real smooth compactly supported $\psi$, with no pointwise Fourier inversion assumption on $u_0$.

source.place: 242-248, combined with LpSpace.lean:81-82,132-139 and SchwartzSpace/Basic.lean:555-567,1131-1133; agent assembly of the two test identities.

proof.text: Put $f=g-u_0$. By step 2, $g$ and $u_0$ are measurable and every point has a neighborhood on which $|g|$ and $|u_0|$ are integrable, so the same holds for $|f|\leq|g|+|u_0|$: $f$ is locally integrable on $U=\mathbf R^m$. For a real smooth compactly supported $\psi$, its support is covered by finitely many such neighborhoods and $|\psi|$ is bounded, so $\psi g$ and $\psi u_0$ are integrable and step 3 gives $\int\psi(x)f(x)\,dx=\int\psi g-\int\psi u_0=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation] with $U=\mathbf R^m$ (open, every compact support lies in it) and this $f$. Thus $f=0$, i.e. $g=u_0$, almost everywhere. In particular $g$ is square integrable and its $L^2$ equivalence class equals the originally specified $u$. Together with step 1 this is the full assertion.

source.place: 205-213 (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, the source of the cited node), applied to the difference; equality of locally integrable functions from compact smooth tests.
